get.description:
General-purpose portfolio instrument: filter and sort one row per client.

The page-level question is "who do I call?" not "what cell is this?". This
endpoint therefore returns the most actionable cell for each client and lets
the caller decide which book view it is looking at via the same filters used
for the saved views: outcome, engagement scope, near-threshold, status, year,
and program.

EVERY CLIENT IN THE BOOK APPEARS, including ones no run has reached yet.
A client absent from the page whose stated job is "who do I call" is the one
client you can be certain nobody calls. Northwind has real payroll and five
locations and used to be invisible here purely because no run had written a
claim for it.

Not-yet-assessed rows carry NULL money rather than zero. Zero reads as "we
looked and found nothing"; null reads as "the pipeline has not reached this
yet", and those must not render alike. They sort as a block after the ranked
rows because they hold no figure to rank on, and the response reports
`assessed_clients` against `total_clients` so coverage is visible before
anyone scrolls. That counter is a DIAGNOSTIC: under the pipeline model a
client sitting unassessed is a gap to close, not a bucket it belongs in.

tools.name: data_catalog
tools.description: What data can be queried: datasets (what one row is), and with `dataset` their columns with meaning, unit, role, sensitivity and the aggregations and filters each allows. `search` narrows by a word in a name or description. Holds no values from the data. Needs no client. Call it before data_query, and never invent a column name: if the catalog has no column for the question, say so.

search.description: A word to find in names and descriptions.

tools.name: data_query
tools.description: Structured, read-only query over ONE client's payroll and enriched calculation data (needs a client). Use it only for questions the fixed tools (client_eligibility, client_trend, client_at_risk, simulate and the rest) cannot answer: descriptive or comparative questions such as an average, a count or a total by location, month, year, designation or method. For anything about the credit figure, eligibility or what the engine concluded, the fixed tools are authoritative; this tool returns exact rows and aggregates from the data, it does not interpret them. Read data_catalog first and use its names exactly, never an invented column; use data_distinct_values to find a location or code before filtering on it. Name every measure with `as` (for example `average_headcount`): the answer refers to a result column by that name. Never write SQL. Prefer an aggregate to a long list: a result is capped (default 100 rows, at most 500) and says when it was cut. Rows that describe individual employees go to the person asking only; Copilot Cowork refuses them unless the user is a writer.

facts.ranking_note: Ordered by what inaction costs, not by size, and in the same order as the page. 'On the line' outranks 'Identified' because a threshold missed at year end is gone, while an unclaimed credit is recoverable retroactively. 'Declining' is a forecast about a year nobody has filed, not a finding against a filed return.
